notes.headline: This master is running +3.2 dBTP over full scale with 11368 runs of clipped samples — it needs a proper limiter ceiling before it goes anywhere.
notes.summary: The biggest issue is level: true peak is +3.2 dBTP, well above full scale, and there are 11368 run(s) of clipped samples starting at 0:01. That's audible distortion now and it will get worse after MP3/AAC encoding. The two are almost certainly the same cause — nothing is holding the ceiling, or something after the limiter is adding gain. Underneath that, integrated loudness is -3.6 LUFS and peak-to-loudness is 6.8 dB, so you're pushing far harder than you need to; Spotify will turn this down about 10.4 dB regardless, and the only thing the extra limiting buys you is lost punch.

priorities.title: Set a real ceiling and stop the clipping
priorities.why: At +3.2 dBTP the file is distorting on playback and will distort further through lossy encoding; the 11368 clipped runs from 0:01 onward are the same problem showing up sample by sample.

priorities.title: Back off the limiting
priorities.why: At -3.6 LUFS with a 6.8 dB peak-to-loudness ratio, streaming turns you down about 10.4 dB anyway — you're paying in transients for loudness nobody hears.

listen_for: The first five seconds (0:01–0:05) on headphones — listen for crackle or grit on the loudest hits once the ceiling is set to −1.0 dB.
Snare and kick attack after lowering Pro Limiter's Input by 2–4 dB, compared at matched volume against the current version.
An MP3/AAC encode of the new bounce on a phone or laptop speaker, checking that the distortion is gone.
Pro Limiter's Integrated LUFS readout across the whole song (F1.3) to confirm where you've landed.
strengths: Left/right balance is 0.01 dB — the image is centered.
Mono loss is only 0.52 dB, so the master holds up on mono playback.
Loudness range of 5.04 LU means the dynamics are consistent across the section.

judge.priority_order: Critical+warning (F1/F2, ceiling/clipping) is placed before the two info-level findings (F3/F4) about over-limiting, matching severity order in the report.
judge.explains_impact: Priority 1 states distortion now and worse after lossy encoding; priority 2 states loss of transients/punch since streaming turns it down anyway.
judge.groups_causes: F1 (true peak) and F2 (clipping) are correctly merged as one ceiling/gain-staging cause, and F3/F4 (loudness and PLR) are merged as one over-limiting cause, matching the report's own overlapping steps.
judge.specific: Notes cite exact figures (-3.6 LUFS, +3.2 dBTP, 11368 runs, 6.8 dB PLR, 10.4 dB turn-down) and the 0:01 timestamp from this bounce.
judge.stage_appropriate: Since stage is 'master', the notes correctly judge loudness/limiting against release/streaming standards rather than treating headroom as a flaw.
judge.faithful: All claims (peak, clipping, loudness, PLR, mono loss, correlation) match the report's measurements without inventing new problems or causes.
judge.concise: The notes stay tightly focused on the two priority clusters and supporting listen-for checks without repetition or filler.
